steps.tx: **Brain metastases** are the most common intracranial tumours in adults, originating primarily from lung cancer 50%, breast cancer 20%, and cutaneous melanoma 10%. Metastatic tumour emboli lodge at grey-white matter junctions and vascular watershed zones where calibre narrows abruptly. Thin-slice contrast-enhanced MRI represents the neuroimaging gold standard, detecting sub-centimetre lesions missed on non-contrast computed tomography.

steps.tx: Ablative focal radiotherapy delivers high local control while sparing uninvolved cerebral parenchyma. **Stereotactic radiosurgery** SRS delivers highly focused, ablative radiation doses in a single fraction to 1 to 4 intact brain metastases, preserving neurocognitive function compared to whole-brain radiation. Randomized trials demonstrate equivalent overall survival and superior learning and memory preservation compared to upfront whole-brain radiotherapy.

left.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS)
points: High ablative dose (16 to 24 Gy in 1 fraction)

steps.tx: Modern whole-brain radiation techniques incorporate neuroprotective strategies to prevent intellectual decline. **Whole-brain radiotherapy** WBRT with hippocampal avoidance and memantine significantly reduces cognitive decline and executive memory deterioration in multiple brain metastases in NRG CC001. Sparing neural stem cells in the subgranular hippocampal dentate zone coupled with NMDA receptor blockade preserves executive memory function without compromising intracranial disease control.

steps.tx: Blood-brain barrier-penetrating targeted therapies have superseded radiotherapy as initial therapy for oncogene-addicted lung cancers. Third-generation EGFR TKI **osimertinib** achieves high central nervous system penetration with intracranial response rates reaching 80% in EGFR-mutant NSCLC brain metastases. Intracranial progression-free survival exceeds fifteen months in FLAURA, often permitting deferral of cranial irradiation.

right.title: 1st/2nd Gen EGFR TKIs (Gefitinib, Afatinib)
points: Subject to P-gp and BCRP efflux pumps
High rate of isolated CNS relapse

steps.tx: Targeted kinase inhibition shows remarkable intracranial activity in HER2-positive breast cancer. **Tucatinib** HER2-selective TKI combined with trastuzumab and capecitabine significantly reduces CNS disease progression and improves overall survival in HER2-positive breast cancer with brain metastases. In the HER2CLIMB trial, the triplet halved the risk of death in patients with active or stable brain metastases.

steps.tx: Subarachnoid tumour dissemination represents a devastating complication carrying grave neurological morbidity. **Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis** is diagnosed by positive cerebrospinal fluid cytology or linear leptomeningeal enhancement on contrast-enhanced spinal and cranial MRI. Clinical presentations feature multifocal neurological deficits, including cauda equina syndrome, cranial nerve palsies, radiculopathy, and communicating hydrocephalus.

rows: Elevated protein (>50 mg/dL), low glucose (<40 mg/dL)

steps.tx: Direct intraventricular chemotherapy bypasses the physiological blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier. **Intrathecal chemotherapy** using preservative-free methotrexate, cytarabine, or liposomal cytarabine via an implanted subcutaneous Ommaya reservoir treats leptomeningeal tumour seeding. Ommaya reservoirs ensure uniform drug distribution throughout ventricular and spinal subarachnoid compartments, avoiding repeated lumbar punctures.

right.title: Lumbar Puncture Injections
points: Post-dural puncture headache and patient discomfort

steps.tx: Rapid alleviation of raised intracranial pressure and peritumoural inflammation is essential. **Dexamethasone** is the primary initial medical therapy for peritumoural vasogenic cerebral oedema, restoring blood-brain barrier integrity and rapidly reversing neurological deficits. Dexamethasone reduces endothelial tight-junction permeability, starting with 4 to 8 mg daily in divided doses, or 16 mg daily in impending herniation with proton pump inhibitor gastroprotection.
